summary: Payment systems and clearing mechanisms are the foundational rails of the global financial architecture, facilitating the secure and efficient transfer of value
lede: Payment systems move funds through initiation, clearing and settlement, while clearing mechanisms determine how payment obligations are resolved. For payment operations, treasury and financial infrastructure professionals, this course addresses managing payment flows and settlement cycles, with practice in mapping legacy messages to structured formats, forecasting intraday liquidity and assessing operational and settlement risks.
audienceIntro: This intermediate-level program is essential for professionals who manage the flow of value and the stability of financial market infrastructures.
audience: Financial Market Infrastructure Specialists focused on RTGS
modules: Foundations of Payment Systems and Infrastructure
Retail Payment Systems and ACH Networks
Digital Innovation and Future Payment Trends
prerequisites: Participants should have at least 2-3 years of experience in banking operations, corporate treasury, or financial technology. A basic understanding of financial accounting and banking transaction flows is required. Familiarity with general risk management concepts is recommended but not mandatory.
topics: Digital financial services, payments & fintech risk
